limitations: Material accuracy, independent forward readback, and scientific novelty are outside this audit.

Archive merge tolerance is box-normalized RMS 1e-5; an event candidate can point to a prior representative. Raw endpoint response and completed fit endpoint are not always separately recorded when merged.
Best-so-far trace records exact paid full-data improvements and material vectors, which supports online data-objective causality.
Physical endpoint scoring inside solver is distinct from post-freeze independent validation, whose receipt was not read.
safe_conclusions: Q6 produced legal distinct proposals and many distant branches, but no direct Q-root update ever improved the global best full-data residual in these four holdouts.
No new Q-root from a coordinate-pre or initial incumbent beat that run coordinate-pre best. ABAR final improvements arose during FullJ corrections of proposed branches.

ABAR improves its fixed eight-sweep coordinate control on three nontrivial cases, but loses all-data residual to native FullJ on each of those cases; this does not establish a specific Q advantage over ordinary restart generation.

GlobalDual changes the material-dependent proposal metric and produces different basins. It reaches the data goal on cases00/03, improves data fit on02, and fails on01 where ordinary FullJ solves immediately.
Original data ranking and charged correction are essential; the dual norm itself is not the likelihood, a completeness certificate, or a ground-truth material metric.
